cases.architecture: Browser page scripts and client components: plain ES modules served from public/, reading location, the fragment, the query string and the referrer, writing to the DOM and navigating with window.location
cases.why: The URL fragment is decoded and written into innerHTML. Anyone can send an invitation-style link whose fragment is markup with an event handler, and it runs in this origin when the page loads; the fragment never reaches the server, so no server-side filter sees it.
The same greeting from the same fragment, but built with createElement and textContent, so the inviter name is rendered as text and never parsed as HTML.

cases.architecture: Browser page scripts and client components: plain ES modules served from public/, reading location, the fragment, the query string and the referrer, writing to the DOM and navigating with window.location
cases.why: After a successful sign-in the page navigates to the next query parameter as given, so a sign-in link on this domain can hand a freshly authenticated user to an attacker's look-alike page.
The same return-after-sign-in flow, but the next parameter is resolved against this origin and discarded unless the result is same-origin, and only its path and query are used.
